terms.definition: A number that describes part of a whole or part of a group.
terms.function: 3/4 says three of four equal parts.
terms.whereItIs: The pizza divided into equal slices with some taken.
terms.whyItMatters: Fractions are the primary way math handles partial amounts.

terms.definition: The top number in a fraction, counting how many parts you have.
terms.function: In 3/4, the 3 counts the slices you take.
terms.whereItIs: The '3' badge above the fraction bar.
terms.whyItMatters: It tells how much of the whole is being described.

terms.definition: The bottom number in a fraction, counting the equal parts the whole is split into.
terms.function: In 3/4, the 4 tells you the whole has 4 equal slices.
terms.whereItIs: The '4' badge below the fraction bar.
terms.whyItMatters: It sets the size of each part — larger denominators mean smaller pieces.

terms.definition: Pieces of a whole that are all the same size.
terms.function: Every slice of the pizza is the same size so 1/4 means the same amount as any other 1/4.
terms.whereItIs: The equal slices cut into the pizza.
terms.whyItMatters: Without equal parts, a fraction would not name a fixed amount.

terms.definition: A fraction of a set — how many items out of the total.
terms.whereItIs: Shown when the fraction counts items rather than slices.
terms.whyItMatters: Fractions describe both split eggs and shared groups.
